chapter: Rhythm Club, studio dates and the 1930s big bands
title: RCA's 23rd Street studio
summary: McRae describes the padded, high-ceilinged RCA studio, where Fats Waller and many others recorded.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Making records: studios, takes and the technology

Did you see the inside
of the RCA studio?

I worked in R -- sure. I
recorded down there.

What kinds of things did
they have, say, in the ceilings? Or, did they have
anything in the ceilings?

They had high ceilings.
I don't know if they used asbestos then, but (inaudible)
sounds were good.
They were padded. Like they used a
cloth padding or something in those days. The rugs
on the floor was padded.
The sounds were great. Because I know --
I did some dates down there (inaudible) some dates
with them. I can't remember now.
But I remember that (little studio) (inaudible) 23rd
